blocks.text:
I need to figure out which atoms count for chain B contacts — whether to include the hetero groups like Zn/Ni labeled as chain B alongside the polymer residues. I'm now looking at the spatial extent of chain A versus chain B coordinates to narrow down where they could be close enough to interact.

I'm tracing which chain A and chain B residues fall into the overlapping x-coordinate range, identifying candidate residue clusters on each side that could plausibly be in contact. Now I'm pulling the detailed atomic coordinates for residue B2611 to check its proximity to the chain A atoms I've flagged.

I'm checking the remaining B-chain residues for proximity and don't find close matches, so now I'm scanning chain A atoms with x-coordinates above -12, starting around residues A2611 and onward.

Comparing coordinates between the two chains, the distances still look too far apart to indicate contact, so I'm narrowing the search to chain A atoms with y-values between -6 and 8 and z-values between 0 and 9 to see if any align with the B2611-2615 region.

I should focus on the actual interface regions instead - chain A's C-terminal stretches against chain B's N-terminal residues, plus checking whether the zinc in chain A sits near anything in chain B's coordinate range. Looking at chain B's y-values, nothing gets close to that zinc site, so I'll work through the contact regions systematically, starting with chain B residues 2611-2615 against the nearby chain A atoms.

I'm scanning through chain A's atoms within a few angstroms of that box, checking each coordinate against chain B's positions - most are too far apart in x, y, or z, but A2611's backbone oxygen looks like it might be close enough to B2615's nitrogen to warrant a closer distance check.

Continuing through A2612 and A2613 side chains and backbone atoms, comparing them against B2614's gamma carbons and nitrogen - a couple pairs come close to the 4Å cutoff but most fall just outside, so I'm moving on to check A2613's own set against the same B reference points.

A2613's N atom turns out to be within contact distance of B2615's N (2.82Å via its O atom), and its O also contacts B2614's C atom at 3.68Å - so A2613 confirms as a valid contact. Now I'm moving to A2614, pulling its backbone coordinates to begin the same nearest-neighbor check.

Checking A2614 against nearby B atoms, most distances come out too large - B2614's N is over 5Å away in z alone, and B2613's C is nearly 4.8Å off. I'm scanning for B atoms with z-coordinates closer to zero to narrow down likely contacts for A2614, starting with comparing its N atom to B2614's N.

Now I'm examining A2615's atom coordinates against B2613's OG position, checking distances to its CA and C atoms to see if they're within contact range.

That distance to C comes out around 3.63, confirming contact, and the O to OG distance also lands close at roughly 2.88, so A2615 is a confirmed contact. I'm also finding B2613 CB contacts A2615 O at about 3.72. Moving on, I'm now listing out A2616's backbone and sidechain coordinates to begin checking its distances next.

Looking further, I check A2616 against chain B residues B2611, B2613, and B2615, finding that A2616 CA to B2611 O comes out to roughly 3.34, confirming contact, and A2616 C to the same oxygen is about 3.52, also a contact — so A2616 counts as well. Now I'm pulling coordinates for A2617 to start the next round of distance checks.

That A2618 check doesn't pan out either—too far from B2611's NH2. I'll move on to scanning A2619 through A2635, since chain B's atoms in that x-range only cover residues around 2611-2615, so I need to see which of these later A residues fall close enough to count as contacts.

Chain B's nearest candidate gives a distance around 5.4, still too far. I'm checking A2622 OG and nearby B2611 NH2 coordinates to see if either falls within range.

Testing NH1 against A2622 OG gives about 3.46 Å, so that's a valid contact. Checking A2622's CB brings it to roughly 4.16, borderline but the OG hit already confirms contact for this residue pair. I'll also scan A2621 and A2623 for any additional nearby atoms, but A2621's oxygen looks too far away based on the y-coordinate difference.

Now I'm checking chain B's CG, CD, NE2, and OE1 atoms against nearby chain A residues like A2615 and A2624, comparing coordinates to spot any contacts within range, but most distances seem too large based on the z-axis differences.

I'm scanning the remaining regions—A2625/A2626 coordinates against chain B's z-range, then checking the chain B and chain A HETATM entries (zinc and nickel ions) for proximity. All these ions appear too far apart from the opposite chain to form meaningful contacts.

Now I'm cross-checking A2612 against B2614's atoms more carefully, confirming the distances stay too large, and re-verifying A2613's close contact holds up. I'm circling back to A2614 to compare each of its atoms against every nearby chain B atom within the relevant coordinate window.

Checking distances from A2614 C to B2613 O gives about 3.73Å, confirming a contact I'd missed, and A2614 CA to the same oxygen comes out around 3.62Å, also within range. Now I want to double-check A2612's distance to that same B2613 oxygen to make sure I'm not missing another contact there too.

Moving on, I'm verifying A2613's nitrogen against B2614's alpha carbon, which comes out to about 5.3Å — already confirmed as contact anyway. I'm now scanning A2611's oxygen against the B2615 residue's backbone atoms, calculating the distance to B2615's oxygen to see if it falls within contact range.

Found it — that distance is 3.66Å, so A2611 does make contact with B2615. I'm checking the carbon and alpha carbon positions too, but those come out too far away. Now I'm pulling in B2616's coordinates to check for additional contacts there.

B2616 turns out to sit right in the interface zone too, so I check its atoms against A2611: the carbon position comes out to 3.59Å, which counts as contact, while the alpha carbon and nitrogen checks land too far away. This tells me I can't just filter by low x-coordinates — I need to systematically check every chain B residue against the chain A boundary atoms.

Looking at the overall geometry, chain A's CA trace runs from around (5.5,9.0,-1.7) at residue 2611 down to (-8.3,-2.0,-8.1) at 2669, while chain B mirrors this from (-9.6,-0.9,4.9) to (8.7,1.1,8.0) — suggesting the two chains relate by a two-fold symmetry with their N-terminal segments crossing near the interface. I'm compiling the full CA coordinate list for chain A to systematically bin atoms by position and find close residue pairs with chain B rather than guessing.

Still generating coordinate data...

Continuing to trace through chain A's CA coordinates, now moving into chain B's list as well.

Looking at chain A, residues near the interface seem to span 2611-2630 plus a few others like 2642-2645 and 2669. Given the dimer's symmetric structure, I'd expect A2611-A2618 to contact B2611-B2617, and by the same symmetry A2622-A2625 should pair with a corresponding region on A's own chain—I need to check this more carefully.

I'm checking distances between A2622-A2625 and nearby chain B residues like B2613, but the gaps are too large to count as real contacts. The B2611 arginine side chain, though, extends far enough that its terminal nitrogens land close to A2622, which matches what I found earlier. Now I'm measuring A2619's backbone and side chain atoms against B2611's guanidinium group to see if there's a second contact point in that same region.

Confirmed that A2618 contact with 3.74 distance. A2617's SG and CB atoms also fall within contact range of B2611's NE, matching what I'd already found. Now moving on to check A2620's contacts.

A2622 shows a plausible contact at 3.46 Å, but A2623 is too far from any chain B atom. I'm now scanning chain A residues near the B2614-B2617 and B2624-B2625 region, checking distances between A2611-A2613 and B2616's side chain atoms, including A2612's OG to B2616's CD1.

Calculating that distance gives just over 4 Å, too far — but A2612 OG to B2616 CE1 comes out to 3.48 Å, confirming a contact for A2612. Checking A2612's CB against the same atom confirms OG is the closer match, and now I'm moving on to check A2611 against B2616/B2617.

Looking at A2611's sidechain geometry and finding that B2616 C to A2611 O is 3.59 Å — a contact. For B2617 N, distances to A2611 N and CA come up too long, but to A2611 O it's 2.82 Å, which confirms another contact.

Now checking A2611 O against B2617 CA, which comes out to 3.74 Å — also a contact. I'm then scanning further down the chain for other residue pairs near B2625, looking at whether A2615/A2616 could be close to B2625's backbone and sidechain atoms given their coordinates.

None of these distances come out close enough though — A2624's CA is too far from B2625. I'm also ruling out B2614's CG1 against A2612/A2613 since the z-distance is too large. Moving on, I want to check whether chain A residues around 2667-2669 have any proximity to chain B atoms in that same spatial region, starting with B2617's SG atom.

Checking A2642-A2645 and A2638-A2640, I'm comparing coordinates to B2612's OG atom, and it looks like A2638's OD1 oxygen is within a couple angstroms of B2612's OG — that's worth flagging as a possible contact.

Testing a few more pairs, OD2 and CG are slightly outside 4 angstroms to OG, but CB on B2612 reaches OD2 at under 4 angstroms, confirming a real contact between A2638 and B2612. Now I need to check A2637 for similar proximity.

Checking A2637's atoms against chain B, the distances all come out too large, so no contact there. Same story for A2639 and A2640 - their coordinates put them too far from chain B's nearest atoms to count. I'm ruling out A2630 through A2635 as well since their x-coordinates are too negative relative to chain B's range.

Now I'm specifically comparing chain A's backbone and side-chain atoms against B2611's CB, CG, CD, and N positions to see if any fall within contact distance. A2619 is too far (over 4 Å combined offset), A2639's CB is clearly off, but A2638's carbonyl carbon is getting close to B2611's nitrogen - within a few angstroms on each axis - so I need to check that pair more carefully.

Checking A2616's ring atoms against B2612's side chain positions, the distances come out too large for contact — around 4.1 Å, beyond the cutoff.

Going through this systematically, I've tallied the chain A contacts so far: 2611, 2612, 2613, 2614, 2615, 2616, 2617, 2618, 2619, 2622, and 2638. Now I'm double-checking a few more residues like A2620 and A2621 against B2611's side chain atoms, but the distances there are too far apart to count as contacts.

I'm also scanning further candidates (A2623-A2626) against nearby B chain atoms, and none of those pass the distance threshold either. Now I'm shifting focus to check whether any chain A atoms fall near the B2616 side chain positions, comparing coordinates to see if anything in chain A reaches into that region of space.

Checking A2611's CG against B2617's CB, I get a distance just over 4.0 (about 4.018), so it narrowly misses the cutoff, but A2611 is already accounted for elsewhere. Next I'm moving on to check A2612's backbone atoms against B2616/B2617.

I don't find anything close for A2612 or A2613 with these B-chain residues, and scanning B2622-2625 against chain A also comes up empty since none of those x/y coordinates line up. So my final list of contacts stands at A2611 through A2619 plus A2622 and A2638, and now I want to verify the A2622 entry specifically.

Recomputing the distance between A2622 OG and B2611 NH1 confirms it's about 3.46 Å apart, well within contact range, while B2611 CZ is slightly farther at 4.41 Å. I also check A2621's oxygen against NH1 but that's too far at 6.3 Å in the y-direction, so nothing new there.

I confirm A2614's contacts at 3.73 and 3.62 Å, and A2615's side chain contacts at 3.63 and 2.88 Å. A2617's N–O contact at 2.74 Å checks out, as does A2616, while A2626 shows no nearby chain B atoms. I'm now scanning whether A2669/A2668 come close to any chain B zinc or other atoms with negative x and z coordinates.

Since B2611-2615 all have positive z values, there's no contact there, which settles the analysis.
